Scope note: This section applies to the Companion Animal Travel Desk team at Aurelia Skyways.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
Purpose: This section sets the basic handling rules for pet travel requests, crate checks, and customer updates so the desk works consistently across shifts.

When a traveler asks to move a pet, the desk reviews the booking, the animal type, and the crate details before anything is confirmed. Staff log every service change in the desk ledger and keep the note short, clear, and current. If a bird is involved, <<FACT F065>> and the booking may continue only if the crate, ventilation, and fit all meet the current acceptance standard. Staff should stay calm, use plain language, and never promise approval before the review is complete.

For service changes, the desk follows a stepwise review. First, confirm the original reservation and the requested change. Next, check whether the crate is suitable, whether the traveler has the needed papers, and whether the route can take the animal without adding risk. If the case is simple, resolve it at the desk and update the ledger at once. If the case is not simple, pass it to the senior coordinator and keep the traveler informed in a steady, respectful way.

When a crate or pet is refused, explain the reason in plain words and record the outcome without blame. If a traveler like Yuki Hernandez or Nikhil Nguyen raises a concern, listen, verify the details, and avoid side talk. If an animal such as Sasha appears distressed, pause the process and follow the safety check before proceeding.

For any unresolved case, contact the senior coordinator or the duty manager for guidance.
